style_when: the story turns on one physical thing — a part, a material, a component, a document — and what that thing costs, contains or crosses a border is the news
prompt: Extreme close-up macro photograph of a brass jeweler's loupe resting on a textured, heavy leather ledger in a dimly lit control room. 100mm macro lens, one razor-sharp focal plane. Shallow depth of field, visible surface texture and dust. Soft directional window light from the left side raking across the brushed brass and deep pine green leather. The loupe and ledger sit off-centre on the thirds, extreme asymmetry with macro focus, the background falling away into graphite shadows. Fine film grain, moody cinematic atmosphere, no people, no legible text.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, numbers, watermark, people, faces, hands
rationale: The story revolves around a single, specific miscalculation: reading the wrong line item on a bill. An extreme close-up of a ledger or invoice under scrutiny perfectly captures the idea of measuring the smallest part and calling it the total.
cue: the smallest part and calls it the total
subject: a heavy leather ledger scrutinized by a brass jeweler's loupe
core_thesis: The six-month AI payback test is being run on token spend rather than business outcome, creating a false metric that passes on cheap routing but fails to measure real ROI.
core_conflict: Measuring token spend vs. measuring actual business process outcome.

title: The Token Spend Trap
